works.abstract: Abstract Background Biodegradable bio-based plastics (BPs) were developed to mitigate environmental plastic pollution, but they generally degrade more readily under aerobic than anaerobic conditions. Aerobic composting produces carbon dioxide, while anaerobic digestion (AD) generates both CO 2 and methane. Because CH 4 is a valuable energy source, enhancing plastic biodegradation under AD conditions could both reduce plastic waste and support fuel production. This study investigates anaerobic gut fungi (AGF) as a biological pretreatment enhancing the biodegradability of different bioplastic designs within AD sludge microbiomes. Results Three AGF-BP pairings were chosen to evaluate the efficacy of AGF pretreatment in improving BP biodegradability in anaerobic sludge. A polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) straw was pretreated with Neocallimastix californiae , while cellulose acetate (CA) and polylactic acid (PLA) films were pretreated with Neocallimastix lanati . Measurements of biogas production, BP weight loss, and surface characterization demonstrated that N. californiae enhanced the biodegradability of PHA and N. lanati enhanced the biodegradability of CA, whereas N. lanati did not significantly improve PLA biodegradability under AD conditions. 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and metatranscriptomic analyses showed that the AGF-pretreated PHA and CA induced significant, BP-specific shifts in the relative abundance of microbial taxa, carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme) transcripts, and other functional genes within the AD microbiome. Furthermore, biogas measurements revealed that N. lanati could partially metabolize CA during the pretreatment phase, but N. californiae could not metabolize PHA. These findings suggest that N. lanati acts through both enzymatic and mechanical mechanisms on CA, while N. californiae likely functions primarily through mechanical disruption of PHA. Transcriptomic analysis of N. lanati during the pretreatment phase further revealed upregulation of cellulolytic CAZymes and adhesion-related genes when grown on CA, suggesting that these factors likely contribute to CA degradation. Conclusions Our findings show for the first time that AGF pretreatment enhances biodegradability of BPs under AD conditions, likely through a synergistic effect of enzymatic hydrolysis and mechanical disruption of the polymer structure. These results highlight AGF as a promising biological pretreatment strategy for enhancing energy recovery and carbon valorization from bioplastic waste streams.
works.title: Anaerobic gut fungi enhance bioplastic degradability under anaerobic digestion conditions
